trueFalse.statement: The story of Chapter 9 begins in the morning when the family wakes up.
trueFalse.explanation: The story begins in the evening: ἑσπέρα ἐστίν — it is evening. James has been on the road all day (ὅλην γὰρ τὴν ἡμέραν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἦν) and has just arrived home.

trueFalse.statement: Magdalene is fifteen years old and helps her mother prepare supper.
trueFalse.explanation: Correct! ἡ δὲ Μαγδαληνή, ἡ θυγάτηρ, ἥτις ἔχει δέκα καὶ πέντε ἔτη, βοηθεῖ τῇ μητρί — Magdalene the daughter, who is fifteen years old, helps her mother.

trueFalse.statement: James tells Peter that his question about whether the river speaks was a foolish one.
trueFalse.explanation: James laughs gently and says: καλῶς ἐρωτᾷς, ὦ τέκνον — you ask well, child. He then clarifies: ἀκούω τοῦ ὕδατος ῥέοντος ἐν τῷ ποταμῷ — I hear the water flowing in the river.

trueFalse.statement: In the wolf story, the donkey was the first to see the wolf.
trueFalse.explanation: Correct! ὁ δὲ ὄνος, βλέπων τὸν λύκον, ἐβόα φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· μόνος γὰρ τὸν λύκον ἔβλεπεν — the donkey, seeing the wolf, was crying out with a loud voice; for he alone was seeing the wolf.

trueFalse.statement: The imperfect indicative expresses a single completed past event.
trueFalse.explanation: The imperfect (ὁ παρατατικός) expresses continuous or habitual past action — 'I was doing' or 'I used to do.' A single completed event is expressed by the aorist (ὁ ἀόριστος). James's farm memories use the imperfect throughout: ἔσκαπτον (I was digging), ἐκοπίων (I was toiling), ἔφερον (I was carrying).

trueFalse.statement: Peter says he wants to be like the shepherd who guards his sheep.
trueFalse.explanation: Peter says the opposite: ἐγὼ θέλω εἶναι ὥσπερ ὁ λύκος! — I want to be like the wolf! He admires the wolf's size and strength: ὁ γὰρ λύκος μέγας ἐστὶν καὶ ἰσχυρός. Everyone laughs.

trueFalse.statement: The supper table in Part B includes honey for the children.
trueFalse.explanation: Correct! ἐπὶ δὲ τῆς τραπέζης ἐστὶν ἄρτος καὶ ἰχθὺς ἐκ τῆς θαλάσσης, καὶ ἐλαῖαι καὶ σῦκα καὶ σταφυλαί· ἔστιν δὲ καὶ γάλα καὶ ὀλίγος οἶνος, καὶ ἔλαιον ἐπὶ τὸν ἄρτον, καὶ μέλι τοῖς παιδίοις — honey for the children is among the items.

trueFalse.statement: In the genitive absolute, the noun and participle are in the genitive and their subject is different from the main clause's subject.
trueFalse.explanation: Correct! The genitive absolute (ἡ γενικὴ ἀπόλυτος) is a participial phrase in the genitive that is grammatically independent from the main clause — its noun is not the subject of the main verb. From Ch9: τοῦ ἡλίου ἀνατέλλοντος (the sun rising) while James was already digging — the sun is not the subject of ἔσκαπτον.

multipleChoice.question: What does ᾖρον mean in: εὑρίσκων τοὺς λίθους ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ ἔσκαπτον καὶ ᾔρον?
options: I had lifted (pluperfect)
I was lifting (continuous past)
I lifted (single completed event)
I lift (habitual present)
multipleChoice.explanation: ᾖρον is the imperfect active indicative 1st singular of αἴρω (to lift, take up). The imperfect marks the action as continuous or repeated in the past: 'I was lifting' the stones repeatedly over time, day after day. It is paired with ἔσκαπτον (I was digging) — two simultaneous, ongoing past actions.

multipleChoice.question: What does the temporal augment do to αἴρω to form ᾖρον?
options: Adds ἔ- before the initial α
Lengthens the initial αι- to ηι-, written ᾖ-
Reduplicates the first consonant
Adds -σ- to the end of the stem
multipleChoice.explanation: αἴρω begins with the diphthong αι-. The temporal augment lengthens this to ηι- (written ᾖ- with iota subscript): αἴρω → ᾖρον. This is the temporal augment (ἡ χρονικὴ αὔξησις) — initial vowels/diphthongs are lengthened rather than having ἔ- added before them.

multipleChoice.question: What does ὅτε ἤμην νέος, ὥσπερ σὺ νῦν mean?
options: Whenever I was young, I was like someone else
When I was young, just as you are now
Because I was young, I acted as you do now
While I am still young, as you see now
multipleChoice.explanation: ὅτε = 'when' (specific past moment); ἤμην = 1sg. imperfect of εἰμί ('I was'); νέος = 'young'; ὥσπερ σὺ νῦν = 'just as you are now.' James draws a comparison between his own boyhood and Peter's current age, making the story personal.

multipleChoice.question: After Peter says he wants to be like the wolf, what does James say he should be instead?
options: A good shepherd like the farmers he met on the road
A child of God — not a beast
A donkey that is faithful and patient
A lamb that stays close to its mother
multipleChoice.explanation: James says with gentleness: σὺ δὲ οὐκ εἶ θηρίον, ἀλλὰ τέκνον θεοῦ — you are not a beast, but a child of God. He then instructs Peter to love his brother, be patient, be gentle and kind, and to control his anger.

multipleChoice.question: What construction is τοῦ δὲ πατρὸς λαλοῦντος, ἡ Μάρθα καὶ ἡ Μαγδαληνή… βλέπουσιν τὰ παιδία?
options: A dative absolute — the noun and participle are in the dative
A genitive absolute — the noun and participle are in the genitive, independent from the main clause
A nominative absolute — the noun is the subject of the main verb
An accusative absolute — the noun is the object of the main verb
multipleChoice.explanation: τοῦ πατρὸς λαλοῦντος is a genitive absolute: τοῦ πατρός (gen.) + λαλοῦντος (gen. masc. sg. present participle). The father (τοῦ πατρός) is not the subject of the main clause — Martha and Magdalene are. The construction sets a background scene while the main action proceeds.

multipleChoice.question: What declension pattern does ἰχθύς, ἰχθύος, ὁ follow?
options: 2nd declension masculine, like λόγος
1st declension masculine, like νεανίας
3rd declension masculine with a υ-stem
3rd declension neuter with a -ματ- stem
multipleChoice.explanation: ἰχθύς is a 3rd-declension masculine noun with a υ-stem. Its forms: nom. ἰχθύς, gen. ἰχθύος, dat. ἰχθύι, acc. ἰχθύν (sg.) and nom. ἰχθύες, gen. ἰχθύων, dat. ἰχθύσι(ν), acc. ἰχθύς (pl.). The genitive ἰχθύος confirms the υ-stem.

fillInTheBlank.prompt: τοῦ ἡλίου _______, ἐγὼ ἤδη ἔσκαπτον τὸν ἀγρόν.
fillInTheBlank.explanation: ἀνατέλλοντος — genitive masculine singular present participle of ἀνατέλλω (to rise). Together with τοῦ ἡλίου, it forms the genitive absolute: 'while the sun was rising.' James began digging even before the sun was fully up.

fillInTheBlank.prompt: χαλεπὸς μὲν _______ ὁ πόνος, ὦ τέκνον, καὶ ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἐκοπίων ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ.
fillInTheBlank.explanation: ἦν — 3rd singular imperfect of εἰμί ('it was'). The imperfect here describes the ongoing state: the labor was difficult (continuously, day after day). James is recounting habitual past conditions on the farm.

ποτήριον (cup) — each person at the supper table has his own cup. ἕκαστος is a pronominal adjective meaning 'each one'; it singles out each individual. The 2nd-declension neuter ποτήριον (nom./acc.) is the object of ἔχει.
